key_insight: Per-string regeneration relaxes CTE need to ~0.999 (64 bits x 3 phases = 192 transfers, <20% loss), achievable by 1970s surface-channel CCDs; NAND tiers give 4-8x density without EUV.
killer_doubt: Poly-Si grain-boundary traps and dark generation (~100 fA fills a 1,000 e- well in ~2 ms); IGZO tail-state deferred charge unmeasured; 100 ns-1 us serial access = capacity tier.
decisive_experiment: University-fab 16-gate IGZO CCD (planar first, then 8-tier vertical): measure CTE versus clock rate, fat zero and 25-85 C, plus dark charge; go if CTE >=0.9995 at 10 MHz. ~$300k.
prior_art: 1970s CCD main/bulk memories (Fairchild, Intel, ~64 kb); our own N-08 vertical oxide CCD (ALIVE-SPEC); no oxide-channel CTE data found in C0 searches.

key_insight: Correct that idle refresh (16-33% of idle power) only needs to protect a few tens of MB of kernel and wake state.
killer_doubt: 180 nm SRAM at ~4.6 um2/bit makes 256 Mb ~1,180 mm2, beyond reticle; LPDDR partial-array self-refresh already refreshes only a chosen segment, no extra die.
decisive_experiment: Phone trace study: standby power with LPDDR5 partial-array self-refresh restricted to a 64 MB segment versus full self-refresh; if PASR captures >90% of savings, the island adds nothing.
prior_art: LPDDR partial-array self-refresh and deep power-down modes; OS suspend-to-disk; Flikker-style critical-data refresh partitioning.

key_insight: AFE back-switching releases 10-20 uC/cm2 at a fixed voltage versus ~2 uC/cm2 linear charge (k=40, 5 nm) in a 0.3 V droop: ~5-10x hold charge without taller pillars.
killer_doubt: Every write of a '1' must exceed the forward switching field, so one full AFE transition per write; need 3e8-7e13 cycles, best AFE ZrO2 seen ~5e9.
decisive_experiment: TiN/ZrO2-rich HZO/TiN MIM coupons (5-8 nm ALD): unipolar cycling to 1e11 at 85 C, measuring plateau hold charge and leakage each decade. ~$150k with university ALD.
prior_art: Our N-01 AFE-reservoir ZrO2 stub (same endurance decision); morphotropic-phase-boundary HZO high-k DRAM dielectric work; AFE hafnia/zirconia energy-storage capacitor literature.

key_insight: A standard interface for error-tolerant memory would let ECC-paid or approximate cells (N-62, N-66) ship across vendors and be procured.
killer_doubt: Uniform 1% BER flips BF16 exponent bits catastrophically, so protected bits must be split out; gain is refresh power and bandwidth (~10-20%), not new bits.
decisive_experiment: Linux MAP_LOSSY patch on an FPGA DRAM tester running an LLM KV cache at relaxed refresh; measure accuracy versus raw BER and refresh savings. <$100k.
prior_art: Flikker (MSR, ASPLOS 2011) critical-data refresh partitioning; EDEN (MICRO 2019) approximate-DRAM DNN inference; RAIDR retention-aware refresh.

key_insight: Effectively a parametron memory: one global pump sustains bistable states in nonlinear accumulation/depletion capacitors, removing refresh controllers and tRFC bandwidth loss.
killer_doubt: Clock energy CV2f: 0.6 fF x (2 V)^2 x 1 kHz = 2.4 pW/cell, ~3x today's refresh (~0.7 pW/bit) unless resonant drive recovers >70%; 6-sigma margin across 1e10 cells.
decisive_experiment: 1-kb IGZO or SKY130 array with off-chip LC-resonant plate drive: map both stable points versus clock amplitude, frequency and temperature; measure hold power per cell and error rate. ~$250k.
prior_art: Goto parametron (1954) global-pump bistables; IBM gated-diode eDRAM cells (~2006); TI tunnel-diode SRAM (~1999) (from memory). Global-clock DRAM self-refresh not verified.

key_insight: Nested shells use both faces of each electrode, and the wide holes needed would only be AR ~8-30, easing the HAR etch.
killer_doubt: Each cell needs >=12-16 nm radial stack, so 4 shells need a >=100-140 nm hole: 18-45F2 per cell at F=12 nm, worse than 6F2.
decisive_experiment: Free first: draw the radial stack with real film thicknesses. If pursued, a 3-shell coaxial MIM in a 200 nm hole tests selective staggered recess of concentric TiN shells.
prior_art: Double-sided cylinder and fin/crown stacked DRAM capacitors (1990s); none found for staggered per-shell ring TFTs.

key_insight: Crested barriers do raise the write/hold current ratio enough on paper (~1e10-1e12 between 3 V and 1 V) for a transistor-free floating-node cell.
killer_doubt: A 20x20 nm floating node holds ~0.005 fF, ~30 e- at 1 V; on a 100 fF crossbar line that is ~50 uV signal under ~200 uV kTC noise.
decisive_experiment: Epitaxial nitride/AlN crested-trilayer coupons: J-V ratio at 3 V vs 1 V and charge-to-breakdown under ns pulses; if >1e8 C/cm2 survives, re-scope as gated floating-node cell (N-10/N-85).
prior_art: Likharev crested/layered tunnel barriers for fast nonvolatile memory (APL ~1998); our N-85 crystalline crested-barrier 1S1C crosspoint.

key_insight: Selector drift as a feature is clever: after firing, Vth rises with log-time, so leakage falls as the bit ages, and each refresh resets it.
killer_doubt: OTS off-current near half-bias is ~pA-nA, 1e3-1e6x above the ~1-13 fA retention budget; ~50 mV/decade drift on a ~250 mV/decade slope buys ~10x.
decisive_experiment: 30 nm OTS devices on a 1 fF on-chip MIM: measure node decay from 0.25-1 V hold over 1 us-10 s after firing, at 85 C; go only if leakage <=10 fA at 0.3 V.
prior_art: Intel/Micron 3D XPoint OTS selectors (drift documented); our N-85/N-87 two-terminal-selector 1S1C crosspoint family.

key_insight: Crowdsourced open-PDK shuttles make hundreds of parallel leakage experiments cheap (~$100s per tile); useful for gain-cell circuit IP and recruiting.
killer_doubt: DRAM tails are GIDL/GIJL in 12 nm buried-wordline BCATs, or <1 aA IGZO; 130-180 nm logic FETs leak by subthreshold/junction paths, so results do not transfer.
decisive_experiment: None worth funding for the DRAM tail; at most one ~$10k Tiny Tapeout gain-cell retention tester to validate the bounty pipeline itself.
prior_art: Tiny Tapeout and open-PDK MPW shuttles (SKY130, GF180, IHP); academic gain-cell eDRAM on open PDKs.

key_insight: Per-module retention profiling turns marginal used DIMMs into usable supply during a ~4x price spike, trading refresh rate for scrap.
killer_doubt: Retired hyperscale DIMMs are mostly DDR4, unusable in DDR5 hosts without CXL; hosts ignore custom SPD refresh fields; refurbished-DIMM resellers already test and resell.
decisive_experiment: Profile 1,000 retired DDR4 RDIMMs at 85 C for retention tail and errors; if <5% need >1x refresh, the passport adds nothing beyond standard refurb testing. ~$100k.
prior_art: Refurbished server-DIMM resellers; Microsoft GreenSKU reusing old DDR4 behind CXL (from memory); CMU REAPER/AVATAR retention profiling.

key_insight: DRAM analog of Intel/Kepler 1T-nC FeRAM: a per-tier oxide Schottky diode replaces ferroelectric coercivity as plate-line selector; clamp-write works one-way; nodes use floating-gate 3D-NAND recess process.
killer_doubt: 0.27 fF tiers share onto a ~1.5 fF pillar (~75 mV signal), forcing a gain-FET read; a ~60 nm hole makes density 2-4x at 16-32 tiers, not 24x.
decisive_experiment: University-fab 4-tier stack in 100-200 nm holes (TiN plates/ZrO2/recessed node/IGZO-RuOx Schottky/pillar): measure clamp-write, read charge, reverse leakage (<20 aA/tier at 85 C), unselected-tier disturb. ~$600k.
prior_art: Intel EP4016625 3D-FRAM plate lines; Kepler Computing 1TnC stacked ferroelectric pillar capacitors (via search snippet); diode-steered linear-capacitor version not found.

key_insight: Display fabs have idle Gen-8.5-10.5 area ~100x cheaper per m2; IGZO TFTs already run there and <1 aA leakage tolerates big, slow cells.
killer_doubt: Production display litho resolves ~1-2 um, not 0.3 um: at F=1.5 um, 20 tiers give ~1.4 TB per Gen-10.5 panel, ~$1.4-5.7/GB, no better than DDR5's $1.48/GB.
decisive_experiment: On a Gen-2/4 research glass line, pattern 0.5 um IGZO 1T1C arrays by NIL or high-res FPD stepper; measure killer-defect density per mask and 4-tier overlay. Break-even needs F<=0.7 um at 20 tiers.
prior_art: SEL (a display company) CAAC-IGZO DOSRAM/NOSRAM, on Si BEOL; our N-36 BEOL cell line on glass carriers; none at Gen-10.5 scale.
